executive_summary: The agent's patch is textually identical to the gold patch and correctly implements payout webhook error consumption. The changes extract failure reasons from connector webhook payloads (specifically Adyenplatform) and conditionally persist them into the payout attempt record only when the status indicates failure. cargo_check passed successfully; the only failing check was rustfmt due to a missing toolchain.

approach_analysis.explanation: The agent's approach matches the gold patch exactly. It introduces a new PayoutWebhookUpdate struct to hold error details, adds an is_payout_failure() helper on PayoutStatus, wires up the IncomingWebhook trait with a defaulted get_payout_webhook_details() method, implements it for Adyenplatform parsing the reason/tracking fields, and updates the router's payouts_incoming_webhook_flow to conditionally populate error_message/error_code only on failure statuses. This is the correct and complete solution.

praised_patterns.observation: Conditional error population only on failure statuses prevents overwriting error fields on non-failure webhooks
praised_patterns.evidence: let payout_attempt_update = if status.is_payout_failure() { ... error_message: payout_webhook_details.error_message ... } else { ... error_message: None ... }

praised_patterns.observation: Default trait implementation ensures backward compatibility for all existing connectors without requiring immediate changes
praised_patterns.evidence: fn get_payout_webhook_details(...) -> CustomResult<PayoutWebhookUpdate, errors::ConnectorError> { Ok(PayoutWebhookUpdate { error_code: None, error_message: None }) }

praised_patterns.observation: Gracefully falls back from data.reason to tracking.reason for robust error extraction
